pages.caption: There was once upon a time a poor miller who had a very beautiful daughter.
pages.scene: [A poor miller's cottage. Sparse furnishings. The signs of poverty are everywhere.]

pages.caption: A beautiful young woman stands in the cottage.
pages.scene: [The miller's daughter. She is very beautiful.]

pages.caption: The miller has come to the palace for an audience with the King.
pages.scene: [The royal palace. A grand hall with a throne at the far end.]

pages.caption: Now it happened one day that he had an audience with the King
pages.scene: [The King sits on his throne. The miller stands before him.]
pages.action: The miller speaks to the King.

pages.caption: In order to appear a person of some importance he told him that he had a daughter who could spin straw into gold.
pages.scene: [The miller stands proudly before the King. He wants to appear important.]

pages.caption: 'Now that's a talent worth having,' said the King to the miller.
pages.scene: [The King leans forward on his throne. He is intrigued.]

pages.caption: 'If your daughter is as clever as you say, bring her to my palace to-morrow, and I'll put her to the test.'
pages.scene: [The King speaks from his throne. He gives a command.]

pages.caption: The miller's daughter is brought to the palace.
pages.scene: [The palace hallway. Guards escort a young woman toward the throne room.]
pages.action: The guards lead the girl through the hallway.

pages.caption: When the girl was brought to him he led her into a room full of straw
pages.scene: [The King stands before the miller's daughter in the palace.]

pages.caption: He led her into a room full of straw.
pages.scene: [The King leads the girl down a corridor. They approach a heavy door.]

pages.caption: A room full of straw. A spinning-wheel and spindle wait.
pages.scene: [A room filled floor to ceiling with straw. A spinning-wheel and spindle sit in the corner.]

pages.caption: Gave her a spinning-wheel and spindle.
pages.scene: [The King holds a spinning-wheel and spindle. He gives them to the girl.]
pages.action: The King gives her the spinning-wheel and spindle.

pages.caption: 'Now set to work and spin all night till early dawn.'
pages.scene: [The King stands at the doorway. He speaks to the girl inside.]

pages.caption: 'And if by that time you haven't spun the straw into gold you shall die.'
pages.scene: [The King's face is stern. He delivers his threat.]

pages.caption: Then he closed the door behind him and left her alone inside.
pages.scene: [The King closes the heavy door. The girl watches from inside.]

pages.caption: She is alone in the room full of straw.
pages.scene: [The girl stands alone in the straw room. The door is shut. She is trapped.]

pages.caption: So the poor miller's daughter sat down, and didn't know what in the world she was to do.
pages.scene: [The girl sits down among the straw. She does not know what to do.]

pages.caption: She hadn't the least idea of how to spin straw into gold
pages.scene: [The girl looks at the straw. She has no idea how to spin it into gold.]

pages.caption: She becomes miserable.
pages.scene: [The girl's face fills with misery. Tears begin to form.]

pages.caption: And became at last so miserable that she began to cry.
pages.scene: [The girl cries in the straw room. Her tears fall on the straw.]

pages.caption: The door opens.
pages.scene: [The door of the straw room. It begins to open.]

pages.caption: Suddenly the door opened, and in stepped a tiny little man
pages.scene: [A tiny little man steps through the doorway. He is small and strange.]

pages.caption: 'Good-evening, Miss Miller-maid; why are you crying so bitterly?'
pages.scene: [The tiny man stands before the crying girl. He looks at her.]

pages.caption: 'I have to spin straw into gold, and haven't a notion how it's done.'
pages.scene: [The girl looks up at the tiny man. She answers him.]

pages.caption: 'What will you give me if I spin it for you?'
pages.scene: [The tiny man asks the girl a question. The spinning-wheel is visible behind them.]

pages.caption: 'My necklace,' replied the girl.
pages.scene: [The girl reaches for her necklace. She offers it to the tiny man.]

pages.caption: The little man took the necklace,
pages.scene: [The tiny man takes the necklace from her hands.]

pages.caption: sat himself down at the wheel
pages.scene: [The tiny man sits down at the spinning-wheel.]

pages.caption: and whir, whir, whir, the wheel went round three times,
pages.scene: [The tiny man begins to spin. The wheel turns.]

pages.caption: and the bobbin was full.
pages.scene: [The bobbin is full of gold. The tiny man stops spinning.]

pages.caption: Then he put on another
pages.scene: [The tiny man puts on another empty bobbin.]

pages.caption: and whir, whir, whir, the wheel went round three times, and the second too was full
pages.scene: [The wheel turns again. The tiny man spins.]

pages.caption: And so it went on till the morning, when all the straw was spun away
pages.scene: [The tiny man continues spinning through the night. Bobbin after bobbin fills with gold.]

pages.caption: and all the bobbins were full of gold.
pages.scene: [Morning light streams through the window. All the bobbins are full of gold. The straw is gone.]

pages.caption: The sun rises over the room of gold.
pages.scene: [The sun rises. Light fills the straw room. Gold glitters on the bobbins.]

pages.caption: As soon as the sun rose the King came
pages.scene: [The King opens the door. He sees the gold.]

pages.caption: and when he perceived the gold he was astonished and delighted
pages.scene: [The King stares at the bobbins of gold. His eyes widen.]

pages.caption: but his heart only lusted more than ever after the precious metal.
pages.scene: [The King's face shows greed. He wants more gold.]

pages.caption: He had the miller's daughter put into another room full of straw, much bigger than the first
pages.scene: [The King leads the girl down a corridor. They approach a second, larger room.]

pages.caption: A second room, much bigger than the first, full of straw.
pages.scene: [A second room, much larger than the first, filled with straw. The girl stands inside.]

pages.caption: and bade her, if she valued her life, spin it all into gold before the following morning.
pages.scene: [The King speaks to the girl from the doorway. He gives his command.]

pages.caption: The girl didn't know what to do
pages.scene: [The girl is alone in the second straw room. She does not know what to do.]

pages.caption: and began to cry.
pages.scene: [The girl begins to cry again.]

pages.caption: Then the door opened as before, and the tiny little man appeared
pages.scene: [The door opens. The tiny little man appears again.]

pages.caption: 'What'll you give me if I spin the straw into gold for you?'
pages.scene: [The tiny man asks the girl his question.]

pages.caption: 'The ring from my finger,' answered the girl.
pages.scene: [The girl pulls the ring from her finger. She holds it out to him.]

pages.caption: The manikin took the ring,
pages.scene: [The tiny man takes the ring from her hand.]

pages.caption: and whir! round went the spinning-wheel again
pages.scene: [The tiny man sits at the spinning-wheel. He begins to spin.]

pages.caption: and when morning broke he had spun all the straw into glittering gold.
pages.scene: [Morning light fills the room. All the straw has been spun into gold.]

pages.caption: The King was pleased beyond measure at the sight.
pages.scene: [The King enters the room. He sees the gold. He is pleased.]

pages.caption: But his greed for gold was still not satisfied.
pages.scene: [The King's face shows insatiable greed. The gold is not enough.]

pages.caption: and he had the miller's daughter brought into a yet bigger room full of straw
pages.scene: [The King leads the girl to a third room. It is the biggest yet, filled with straw.]

pages.caption: The third room. The biggest yet. Full of straw.
pages.scene: [The third room. Enormous. Straw fills every corner. The girl stands small in the middle.]

pages.caption: 'You must spin all this away in the night'
pages.scene: [The King speaks to the girl. He makes his offer.]

pages.caption: 'But if you succeed this time you shall become my wife.'
pages.scene: [The King continues speaking. He promises her something.]

pages.caption: 'She's only a miller's daughter, it's true,' he thought
pages.scene: [The King thinks to himself. He considers her as a wife.]

pages.caption: 'But I couldn't find a richer wife if I were to search the whole world over.'
pages.scene: [The King continues thinking. He could not find a richer wife.]

pages.caption: When the girl was alone the little man appeared for the third time
pages.scene: [The girl is alone in the third straw room. The door is closed.]

pages.caption: The tiny man appears for the third time.
pages.scene: [The tiny man appears for the third time. He stands before the girl.]

pages.caption: 'What'll you give me if I spin the straw for you once again?'
pages.scene: [The tiny man asks the girl his question.]

pages.caption: 'I've nothing more to give,' answered the girl.
pages.scene: [The girl answers. She has nothing left to give.]

pages.caption: 'Then promise me when you are Queen to give me your first child.'
pages.scene: [The tiny man makes his demand. He wants her firstborn child.]

pages.caption: 'Who knows what may not happen before that?' thought the miller's daughter
pages.scene: [The girl thinks to herself. She considers her situation.]

pages.caption: and besides, she saw no other way out of it
pages.scene: [The girl sees no other way out. She is trapped.]

pages.caption: so she promised the manikin what he demanded
pages.scene: [The girl promises the tiny man. She gives her word.]

pages.caption: and he set to work once more and spun the straw into gold.
pages.scene: [The tiny man sits at the spinning-wheel. He begins to spin for the third time.]

pages.caption: When the King came in the morning
pages.scene: [Morning. The King enters the third straw room. Gold fills the room.]

pages.caption: and found everything as he had desired
pages.scene: [The King looks at the gold. Everything is as he desired.]

pages.caption: he straightway made her his wife
pages.scene: [The King speaks to the miller's daughter. He makes her his wife.]

pages.caption: and the miller's daughter became a queen.
pages.scene: [The miller's daughter wears a crown. She is now a queen.]

pages.caption: When a year had passed
pages.scene: [The palace. A year passes. Seasons change outside the windows.]

pages.caption: a beautiful son was born to her
pages.scene: [A newborn baby. A beautiful son. The Queen holds him.]

pages.caption: and she thought no more of the little man
pages.scene: [The Queen gazes at her baby. She is happy. She has forgotten the tiny man.]

pages.caption: She has forgotten her promise.
pages.scene: [The Queen plays with her son. She has forgotten her promise.]

pages.caption: The Queen is alone with her baby.
pages.scene: [The Queen's chamber. She is alone with her baby.]

pages.caption: till all of a sudden one day he stepped into her room
pages.scene: [The door opens. The tiny little man steps into the room.]

pages.caption: 'Now give me what you promised.'
pages.scene: [The tiny man stands before the Queen. He speaks.]

pages.caption: The Queen is horrified. She remembers.
pages.scene: [The Queen's face fills with terror. She remembers her promise.]

pages.caption: The Queen was in a great state, and offered the little man all the riches in her kingdom
pages.scene: [The Queen offers the tiny man riches. She begs him.]

pages.caption: if he would only leave her the child.
pages.scene: [The Queen continues pleading. She wants him to leave the child.]

pages.caption: 'No, a living creature is dearer to me than all the treasures in the world.'
pages.scene: [The tiny man refuses. He wants the child.]

pages.caption: Then the Queen began to cry
pages.scene: [The Queen begins to cry.]

pages.caption: and sob so bitterly
pages.scene: [The Queen sobs bitterly. Her grief is deep.]

pages.caption: that the little man was sorry for her
pages.scene: [The tiny man watches the Queen cry. He feels sorry for her.]

pages.caption: 'I'll give you three days to guess my name'
pages.scene: [The tiny man speaks. He gives her a chance.]

pages.caption: 'and if you find it out in that time you may keep your child.'
pages.scene: [The tiny man finishes his offer. She must guess his name.]

pages.caption: Then the Queen pondered the whole night over all the names she had ever heard
pages.scene: [Night. The Queen sits alone. She thinks of every name she has ever heard.]

pages.caption: and sent a messenger to scour the land
pages.scene: [The Queen sends a messenger out into the world.]

pages.caption: and to pick up far and near any names he could come across.
pages.scene: [The messenger rides out. He is to find names far and near.]

pages.caption: When the little man arrived on the following day she began with Kasper, Melchior, Belshazzar
pages.scene: [The next day. The tiny man arrives at the palace.]

pages.caption: and all the other names she knew, in a string
pages.scene: [The Queen lists all the names she knows. She speaks them one after another.]

pages.caption: but at each one the manikin called out
pages.scene: [The tiny man replies to each name. He denies them all.]

pages.caption: 'That's not my name.'
pages.scene: [The tiny man speaks his reply.]

pages.caption: The next day she sent to inquire the names of all the people in the neighborhood
pages.scene: [The second day. The Queen sends out messengers to the neighborhood.]

pages.caption: and had a long list of the most uncommon and extraordinary for the little man
pages.scene: [The messengers return with a long list of names.]

pages.caption: 'Is your name, perhaps, Sheepshanks Cruickshanks, Spindleshanks?'
pages.scene: [The tiny man arrives. The Queen reads from the list.]

pages.caption: But he always replied: 'That's not my name.'
pages.scene: [The tiny man denies the names again.]

pages.caption: On the third day the messenger returned and announced
pages.scene: [The third day. The messenger returns to the palace.]

pages.caption: 'I have not been able to find any new names'
pages.scene: [The messenger speaks to the Queen. He has news.]

pages.caption: 'But as I came upon a high hill round the corner of the wood'
pages.scene: [The messenger describes his journey. He came upon a high hill.]

pages.caption: 'Where the foxes and hares bid each other good-night, I saw a little house'
pages.scene: [The messenger describes what he saw. Foxes and hares. A little house.]

pages.caption: 'In front of the house burned a fire, and round the fire sprang the most grotesque little man, hopping on one leg'
pages.scene: [A fire burns in front of a little house. A grotesque little man dances around it.]

pages.caption: 'and crying: To-morrow I brew, to-day I bake'
pages.scene: [The tiny man dances and sings. He cries out a rhyme.]

pages.caption: 'And then the child away I'll take; For little deems my royal dame'
pages.scene: [The tiny man continues his rhyme. He will take the child.]

pages.caption: 'That Rumpelstiltzkin is my name!'
pages.scene: [The tiny man reveals his name in the rhyme.]

pages.caption: You can imagine the Queen's delight at hearing the name
pages.scene: [The Queen hears the name. She is delighted.]

pages.caption: She knows his name.
pages.scene: [The Queen smiles. She knows his name now.]

pages.caption: When the little man stepped in shortly afterward and asked: 'Now, my lady Queen, what's my name?'
pages.scene: [The little man steps into the Queen's room. He asks for her answer.]

pages.caption: 'Is your name Conrad?'
pages.scene: [The Queen asks the first name. She is calm.]

pages.caption: 'No.'
pages.scene: [The tiny man replies.]

pages.caption: 'Is your name Harry?'
pages.scene: [The Queen asks the second name.]

pages.caption: 'No.'
pages.scene: [The tiny man replies again.]

pages.caption: 'Is your name perhaps, Rumpelstiltzkin?'
pages.scene: [The Queen asks the true name. She is confident.]

pages.caption: 'Some demon has told you that! some demon has told you that!'
pages.scene: [The tiny man screams. His face twists with rage.]

pages.caption: He drives his right foot into the ground.
pages.scene: [The tiny man drives his right foot into the ground.]
pages.action: He drives his foot into the ground.

pages.caption: His foot sinks in up to his waist.
pages.scene: [His foot sinks into the ground up to his waist.]

pages.caption: He seizes his left foot with both hands.
pages.scene: [In a passion, the tiny man seizes his left foot with both hands.]

pages.caption: He tears himself in two.
pages.scene: [The tiny man tears himself in two.]

pages.caption: The Queen is alone. Her child is safe.
pages.scene: [The Queen stands alone in her chamber. The tiny man is gone.]
